proposals.provenance_note_verbatim: Proposition 2 - AI-Induced Epistemic Scarcity Shift. In the positive-backlog regime, a general AI capability improvement increases unresolved validation workload if and only if its marginal effect on effective candidate workload exceeds its marginal effect on validation capacity. Deliberately symmetric: permits generation-dominant (backlog rises), balanced (unchanged), and validation-dominant (backlog falls) outcomes.

proposals.provenance_note_verbatim: Proposition 3 - Bottleneck Revaluation. When the validation constraint binds and sufficiently valuable unprocessed candidates exist, the marginal social value of resources that expand mu is positive; a technology that expands candidate supply without proportionately expanding mu can raise the shadow value of contributory expertise, interactional translation, world access, verification infrastructure, and reviewer attention even while lowering the marginal cost of producing plausible answers. Concerns constrained capability, not observed wages.

proposals.drift_note: Appendix A of the source manuscript states this equation's provenance only as 'Present framework' (no cited Toledo code). Per this extraction task's instruction, rootless 'present framework' equations are rooted at weld and read through the domain-weld requirement weld/M.02.v1 (itself Eq.(1) of this same manuscript, already registered as an economics-domain instantiation of that requirement) rather than left as an HRP-X rootless placeholder. This is a disclosed convention, not a demonstrated direct reading of weld/M.02.v1's own statement.

occurrences.evidence: Ledger row (1): 'Economics-domain commuting requirement | Domain instantiation | Toledo domain-weld requirement'. Manuscript sec.4.2 states q_{D,t+1} o F_t = F#_{D,t} o q_{D,t} verbatim-structurally identical to CAN-006's q_{D,n+1}∘F_n = F#_{D,n}∘q_{D,n}, with its own status line reading 'Status: economics-domain instantiation of the Toledo domain-weld requirement; not a new Toledo theorem.'

Ledger row (2): 'K_like^AI != K_validated | Existing non-collapse | Toledo CAN-062 lineage'. Manuscript's K_like^{AI} \neq K_{validated} (secs.1, 4.3, 23) is verbatim-identical (up to notation AI(Q)=K_like) to CAN-062's statement 'AI(Q)=K_like, K_like ≠ K_validated'.

Ledger row (3): 'AI-assisted performance != retained human capability | Existing non-collapse / interpretation | Toledo Human Return lineage'. Manuscript's categorical statement (sec.4.3) restates the same non-collapse CAN-074 states in delta form (ΔPerformance_AI>0 ⇏ ΔH_return>0, equivalently 'Assisted performance ≠ Unaided Human Return'); the manuscript's own Eq.(27) later gives the exact delta form (see equation 27 occurrence below).

Ledger row (6): 'K_S^A=(Tr_A,Str_A,Cap_A) | Existing knowledge architecture | Toledo knowledge-admission / knowledge-triple lineage'. registry/EQ_LIBRARY.md line 1361 and registry/CANONICAL_MAP.md line 440 both map the raw record eq_19640361.json ('K_S^A = (Tr_A, Str_A, Cap_A)', 'Knowledge (Df) formalized as a triple: trace residue Tr_A, coherent usable structure Str_A, and generative capacity Cap_A') to weld/E.03.v1; CAN-031's own statement.latest has since been revised (BBL-172 latest-formulation-wins) to a more elaborate admission-status formula sigma_K(p)=Admit_E(...), so this is the same admitted object under a later, more developed statement, not a verbatim string match against CAN-031's current text.

Ledger row (26): 'Human Return <C,T,S,A> | Existing definition | Toledo Human Return lineage'. Manuscript's R_H^{return}=⟨C,T,S,A⟩ (sec.10) is verbatim-identical to CAN-077's statement 'R^return_H = ⟨C, T, S, A⟩'.

Ledger row (27): 'Assisted performance does not imply Human Return | Existing non-collapse | Toledo'. Manuscript's ΔPerformance_{AI}>0 \not\Rightarrow \Delta R_H^{return}>0 (sec.10) is verbatim-identical in form to CAN-074's statement 'ΔPerformance_AI>0 ⇏ ΔH_return>0 (equivalently: Assisted performance ≠ Unaided Human Return)'.

Ledger row (30): 'Protocol burden tuple | Existing definition | Toledo'. Manuscript's B^{use}=⟨Time,CognitiveLoad,VerificationCost,Interruption,LiteracyDemand⟩ (sec.19.5) is verbatim-identical to CAN-200's statement 'B^use=⟨Time,CognitiveLoad,VerificationCost,Interruption,LiteracyDemand⟩; Epistemically optimal ≢ Behaviorally adoptable'.

phi_check.method: keyword/substring screen over registry/CANONICAL.json's name and statement.latest fields for each new construct's own distinguishing names/symbols (Lambda_t, mu_t candidate-validation-capacity pairing, B_{t+1} backlog recursion with delta_B exit rate, chi_i(Q,D,t) expertise-state enum, Core Epistemic Registration R_p tuple, Y_{K,t} validated-value gate sum, shadow-value Lagrangian on Phi(mu,C), university Pareto-portfolio over {Y_K, Delta R_H^return, W, T, N_v}), plus a manual read of the closest thematically-related existing entries (weld/E.*, weld/H.*, A.8/M.15.v1 'material feasibility and portfolio capacity constraints', RUS-0002/RUS-0003 Lagrangian/Hamiltonian readings, CAN-194).
phi_check.result: No existing CANONICAL.json entry found structurally equivalent under the phi-criterion (renaming / fixed positive scale / fixed constant substitution, same shared domain, no limits or approximations) to any of the 16 new proposals in this file. The nearest keyword hits (A.8/M.15.v1's budget-line portfolio constraint; RUS-0002/RUS-0003's discrete-retention Lagrangian/Hamiltonian; RUS-0051's QCD vacuum-angle Lagrangian) are different objects in different domains (research-project budget accounting; a physics field-theory Lagrangian/Hamiltonian pair; a QCD CP-violation term) with no renaming/scale/constant-substitution bijection to the economics candidate-validation-backlog constructs.
phi_check.caveat: This is a keyword/manual screen over 946 entries, not an exhaustive machine-checked equivalence search (same caveat as registry/proposals/effort_v0_3.json's own phi-check note) — treat 'no match found' as a Dr-tier readout of this screen, not a proof of non-existence.
